description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Provides types supporting the measurement and comparison of date and time periods, including:
- TZ Database
- Unix time
- DOS date/time
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes:
- The packages no longer have a `net8.0` build. An application on .NET 8 or .NET 9 gets a .NET Standard build, without the APIs that only the `net10.0` build has, such as `DateOnly` and `TimeOnly` support. To keep those APIs, move the application to .NET 10.
- The `netstandard1.x` and `netstandard2.0` builds no longer list `JetBrains.Annotations` as a NuGet dependency. If your code uses its attributes and you got the package through DataStandardizer, add a reference to `JetBrains.Annotations` to your project.
- `TzDataTimezoneAttribute` and the `TzDataExtensions.GetComment`, `GetIsoCountryCodes`, `GetLatitude` and `GetLongitude` methods are removed; use the `Comment`, `IsoCountryCodes`, `Latitude` and `Longitude` properties of `TzDataTimezone`.
- The explicit conversion from `string` to `TzDataTimezone` returns the predefined time zone, or the canonical one for a deprecated name, and throws `InvalidCastException` for an unknown identifier or `null`.
- `default(TzDataTimezone)` is `Etc/UTC`, equal to the new `TzDataTimezone.Etc.UTC` field: it converts to `"Etc/UTC"` instead of `null`, `ToString()` returns `"UTC"`, and its members return the zone lines, location and offsets of `Etc/UTC` instead of throwing `InvalidOperationException`.
- The conversion from `uint` to `DosDateTime` is explicit, and throws `InvalidCastException` for a packed value that isn't a valid DOS date and time.
- `ToDateTimeOffset(TzDataTimezone, TzDataLocalTimeResolution)` now rejects the result of `UnixTime.ToDateTime`, which is of kind `Utc`; use `TzDataTimezone.GetUtcOffset` and the other instant-based extensions for it.
- `DateTime.ToUnixTime` throws `ArgumentException` for a `DateTime` of kind `Local`, instead of reading its fields as UTC; call `ToUniversalTime` first.

New:
- `TzDataTimezone.Parse`, `TryParse` and the explicit conversion accept `Etc/UTC` and the deprecated names linked to it, such as `UTC` and `Zulu`.
- `IcalTimeZoneResolver.TzData` resolves the TZIDs `Etc/UTC`, `UTC`, `Zulu` and the other names the TZ Database links to `Etc/UTC`, with an offset of 0.
- `SystemTimeWithGregorianCalendar` implements `IEquatable<SystemTimeWithGregorianCalendar>`.
- `TzDataTimezone.Etc.GMT`, the TZ Database's `Etc/GMT` zone.

Fixed:
- Debuggers can step into the packages' source through Source Link.
- `TzDataTimezone.CompareTo` orders time zones by identifier instead of throwing `ArgumentException`.
- `ToDateTimeOffset` on a `DateTime` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`, not `ArgumentException` "falls in a gap", when the instant of the local time falls outside the range of `DateTime`.
- `UnixTime`, `DosDateTime` and other system times no longer lose a whole second for many values in `ToDateTime`, `ToTimeOnly` and `SystemTimeWithGregorianCalendar.Second`.
- `DateTime.ToUnixTime` no longer returns a value a second early for many times of day.
- A `UnixTime` millions of years from the epoch throws `OverflowException` from `ToDateTime` and the `SystemTimeWithGregorianCalendar` date members, instead of giving a wrong date.
- `DosDateTime` constructors throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for a day past the end of its month, or a packed value that isn't a valid DOS date and time, instead of failing later from `JulianDayNumber`.
- `JulianDayNumber` of a default `DosDateTime` throws `InvalidOperationException`.
- A default SystemTimeWithGregorianCalendar throws InvalidOperationException instead of NullReferenceException.
- `TzDataTimezone.Parse`, `TryParse` and the explicit cast from `string` accept `GMT`, `Greenwich` and the other names that the TZ Database links to `Etc/GMT`, and return `TzDataTimezone.Etc.GMT`.
- `UnixTime.ToDateTime`, and `ToDateTime` on a `SystemTimeWithGregorianCalendar` that wraps a `UnixTime`, return a `DateTime` of kind `Utc`, so `ToUniversalTime` and `DateTimeOffset` no longer apply the machine's offset to it.

Changed:
- The netstandard1.x and netstandard2.0 builds now carry nullable annotations, so projects on C# 8 or later with nullable enabled get null warnings from them.
- `IcalTimeZone.FromTzData` defines `Etc/UTC` for `default(TzDataTimezone)` instead of throwing `InvalidOperationException`.
